predictions.selection_reason: document.location.href (attacker-controlled URL) -> regex extraction -> sets global logging level, influencing debug output and potentially exposing sensitive information
predictions.source_summary: document.location.href (full URL including query parameters) is parsed via regex /logging=([A-Za-z0-9\._\-]*)/ to extract the logging parameter value. The URL is attacker-controlled as it can be crafted by users.
predictions.sink_summary: The extracted value directly sets Util._log_level global variable, which controls the verbosity of console logging functions (Util.Debug, Util.Info, Util.Warn, Util.Error) throughout the application via Util.init_logging().
predictions.guard_summary: No validation of the extracted logging level value beyond regex character class [A-Za-z0-9\._\-]. The regex allows arbitrary strings matching this pattern, which are passed to Util.init_logging() where invalid values throw an exception. No authentication, authorization, or access controls on URL parameter parsing.
predictions.risk_pattern: Attacker-controlled URL parameter directly controls application-wide debug logging verbosity without access controls, potentially exposing sensitive debug information through browser console.
predictions.context_summary: The function WebUtil.init_logging() is called immediately after definition (line 47), setting log level at page load. Util.init_logging() configures console logging functions based on _log_level value: 'debug' enables all logging, 'info' enables info/warn/error, 'warn' enables warn/error, 'error' enables only error, 'none' disables all. Logging functions output application state, connection details, errors, and debugging information.
unresolved_facts: Whether debug logging exposes authentication credentials, session tokens, or other highly sensitive secrets (only saw connection URIs, browser info, and error details in evidence)
Whether the exception thrown for invalid logging values could be leveraged for other attacks
Whether logging output is accessible to attackers in production deployment scenarios

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: attacker-controlled URL parameter directly controls application logging level without validation, potentially exposing sensitive debug information
